title: Projects
text: A selection of what I’m working on now. I keep two GitHub accounts. My work for NOAA’s Northeast Fisheries Science Center is done under my work account, MGrezlik, and much of it lives in the Ecosystem Dynamics and Assessment Branch organization, NOAA-EDAB. This website and my personal and past research projects live on my personal account, MaxGrezlik.

title: Projects
text:
Current work


State of the Ecosystem
I automate and maintain several of the ecosystem indicators in the annual State of the Ecosystem reports for the New England and Mid-Atlantic Fishery Management Councils, which give managers a yearly summary of ecosystem conditions.
ecodata · NEFMC report · MAFMC report · Technical docs


Thermal habitat suitability indicator
For the New England Fishery Management Council’s Risk Policy, I developed an indicator of thermal habitat suitability that tracks how ocean temperatures are changing the habitat available to managed species. It will appear in this year’s State of the Ecosystem report.
In development

title: Projects
text:
R packages I maintain


Rpath
An R implementation of the Ecopath with Ecosim food web model, used to build mass-balance ecosystem models and simulate them over time. My work includes fitting Rsim, its dynamic simulation component, to observed time series.
Documentation · GitHub


survdat
Pulls and processes data from the NEFSC bottom trawl surveys, with tools for calculating stratified means and other survey-based indices.
Documentation · GitHub


comlandr
Pulls and processes commercial fishery landings data for the Northeast US, preparing them for use in assessments and ecosystem models.
Documentation · GitHub

title: Projects
text:
Past research


Georges Bank portfolio management
Portfolio-theory explorations using the GBRpath ecosystem model to support ecosystem-based management of Georges Bank fisheries.

title: Max Grezlik
text:
Fishery Data Analyst · NOAA Northeast Fisheries Science Center
I’m a fisheries scientist with a passion for data-driven solutions in marine conservation and resource management. My work bridges the gap between ecological research and applied fisheries science, with a strong focus on quantitative methods, ecosystem based fisheries management, and sustainable fisheries.
I regularly use R, RStudio, and GitHub to build tools, analyze complex datasets, and communicate findings. This site is a hub for my current projects, publications, and CV.
See what I’m working on now on the Projects page. You can find my code on GitHub in two places: work for NOAA’s Northeast Fisheries Science Center is on my work account, MGrezlik, and personal projects, including this site, are on MaxGrezlik.
Whether you’re a collaborator, a fellow scientist, or just curious about fisheries research, welcome!
